Public hosted zones with all private records copied
Resolver outbound endpoints with forwarding rules to on-premises
Resolver inbound endpoints for on-premises queries to AWS

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Hybrid DNS needs inbound endpoints for on-premises-to-AWS queries and outbound endpoints for AWS-to-on-premises queries.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Internet gateways attached to every VPC in…: IGWs are unrelated.
• Public IP addresses for all DNS resolvers on…: Public resolver IPs are unnecessary.
• Public hosted zones with all private records…: Public zones expose records.

Key takeaway: Hybrid DNS needs both inbound and outbound endpoints.

stem: A company wants to log DNS queries made by resources in its VPCs for security analysis. Which feature fits?

choices.text: Route 53 Resolver query logging
Route 53 traffic flow policies
Route 53 public DNSSEC signing
Route 53 health check alarms

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Resolver query logging records DNS queries from VPCs to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Firehose.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Route 53 traffic flow policies: Traffic flow manages routing.
• Route 53 public DNSSEC signing: DNSSEC signs public zones.
• Route 53 health check alarms: Health checks monitor endpoints.

Key takeaway: Log VPC DNS queries with Resolver query logging.

stem: An on-premises DNS server forwards queries for a private hosted zone to a Resolver inbound endpoint, but queries fail. Which TWO checks are most relevant? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The VPC's DNS support attribute is disabled for security
The inbound endpoint is placed in a subnet without routes
The private hosted zone is associated with the VPC containing the inbound endpoint
The private hosted zone is converted to a public hosted zone for on-premises use
Security groups on the inbound endpoint allow DNS traffic from on-premises

explanation:
Why this is correct:
The zone must be associated with the endpoint's VPC, and endpoint security groups must allow TCP/UDP 53 from on-premises.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The VPC's DNS support attribute is disabled…: DNS support must be enabled.
• The inbound endpoint is placed in a subnet…: Endpoints need network reachability.
• The private hosted zone is converted to a…: Public zones are not required.

Key takeaway: Check zone association and endpoint security groups.

stem: A network team wants VPCs, subnets, route tables, and transit gateway attachments deployed consistently across accounts. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Infrastructure as code with CloudFormation StackSets or Terraform through pipelines
A shared document listing settings that each account owner applies by hand
Copying screenshots of a reference VPC into each new account's wiki page
Manual configuration in the console by different engineers in each account

explanation:
Why this is correct:
IaC deployed through pipelines ensures consistent network configuration across accounts.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A shared document listing settings that each…: Documents do not enforce consistency.
• Copying screenshots of a reference VPC into…: Screenshots are not deployable.
• Manual configuration in the console by…: Manual setup drifts.

Key takeaway: Automate networks with IaC.

stem: When a new VPC attachment is created, it must be associated automatically with the correct transit gateway route table based on tags. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Asking application teams to email the network team after creating attachments
An EventBridge rule on attachment creation invoking a Lambda function that sets associations
A weekly review by the network team that fixes route table associations by hand
Enabling default route table association for every attachment in all environments

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Event-driven automation applies tag-based association rules as soon as attachments are created.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Asking application teams to email the…: Email requests are manual.
• A weekly review by the network team that…: Weekly reviews are slow.
• Enabling default route table association for…: Default association ignores environment segmentation.

Key takeaway: Automate TGW associations with events.

stem: A company wants a central dashboard of its global network topology, including transit gateways and on-premises sites. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon Macie
AWS Artifact
AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Network Manager

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Network Manager visualizes and monitors global networks built on transit gateways and Cloud WAN.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon Macie: Macie finds sensitive data.
• AWS Artifact: Artifact provides compliance documents.
• AWS Cost Explorer: Cost Explorer analyzes costs.

Key takeaway: Visualize global networks with Network Manager.

stem: A company wants on-premises applications to reach S3 over Direct Connect privately without traversing the internet. Which TWO options fit? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A Route 53 public hosted zone for S3 names
A second internet gateway on the same VPC
A private VIF to a VPC with an S3 interface endpoint
A NAT gateway in a public subnet of the VPC
A public VIF to reach S3 public endpoints over DX

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Public VIFs reach AWS public endpoints over DX, and interface endpoints expose S3 privately in a VPC reachable over a private VIF.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A Route 53 public hosted zone for S3 names: Public zones do not route traffic.
• A second internet gateway on the same VPC: A VPC has one IGW.
• A NAT gateway in a public subnet of the VPC: NAT gateways send traffic to the internet.

Key takeaway: Reach S3 over DX via public VIF or interface endpoints.

stem: EC2 instances in a private subnet must access S3 without NAT charges. Which endpoint type is the lowest-cost option?

choices.text: NAT gateway route
S3 interface endpoint
Internet gateway route
S3 gateway endpoint

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Gateway endpoints for S3 have no hourly or data processing charges.

Why the other options are wrong:
• NAT gateway route: NAT adds charges.
• S3 interface endpoint: Interface endpoints have hourly and data charges.
• Internet gateway route: IGWs require public addressing.

Key takeaway: Lowest-cost private S3 access → gateway endpoint.

stem: On-premises clients over Direct Connect must reach S3 through a VPC endpoint. Why won't a gateway endpoint work?

choices.text: Gateway endpoints require a public VIF before they can be created
Gateway endpoints are reachable only from within the VPC, not from on-premises networks
Gateway endpoints support only DynamoDB traffic and never accept any S3 requests from clients
Gateway endpoints are regional and cannot be used by any EC2 instance

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Gateway endpoints work through VPC route tables and cannot be reached from on-premises; interface endpoints can.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Gateway endpoints require a public VIF…: No public VIF is required.
• Gateway endpoints support only DynamoDB…: Gateway endpoints support S3 and DynamoDB.
• Gateway endpoints are regional and cannot be…: EC2 instances in the VPC use them.

Key takeaway: On-premises access to S3 via VPC → interface endpoints.

stem: A company uses Direct Connect and wants to use AWS BGP communities to control how far its routes are propagated within AWS on a public VIF. Which feature fits?

choices.text: MED values set on routes advertised to AWS over the VIF
Local preference communities on routes received from AWS
Scope communities such as 7224:9100 on advertised prefixes
AS_PATH prepending on routes advertised by AWS to customers

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Public VIF scope communities (for example, 7224:9100 for the local Region) control propagation of customer routes within AWS.

Why the other options are wrong:
• MED values set on routes advertised to AWS…: MED is not used for scope control.
• Local preference communities on routes…: Local preference communities influence AWS's path selection on private or transit VIFs.
• AS_PATH prepending on routes advertised by…: Customers cannot prepend AWS's routes.

Key takeaway: Control public VIF route scope with communities.

stem: Instances in a VPC need IPv6 outbound internet access without allowing inbound IPv6 connections. Which component fits?

choices.text: Egress-only internet gateway
Transit gateway attachment only
NAT gateway in a public subnet
Virtual private gateway only

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Egress-only internet gateways allow outbound IPv6 while blocking inbound connections.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Transit gateway attachment only: TGWs route between networks.
• NAT gateway in a public subnet: NAT gateways are for IPv4 translation.
• Virtual private gateway only: VGWs connect VPNs.

Key takeaway: Outbound-only IPv6 → egress-only IGW.

stem: Resolver forwarding rules must be shared with 40 accounts in an OU. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Recreate the rules manually in each account
Put the rules in a public hosted zone
Share the rules with the OU through RAM
Copy the rules into DHCP option sets

explanation:
Why this is correct:
RAM shares Resolver rules with accounts or OUs, which then associate them with VPCs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Recreate the rules manually in each account: Manual recreation drifts.
• Put the rules in a public hosted zone: Public zones are unrelated.
• Copy the rules into DHCP option sets: DHCP options do not contain Resolver rules.

Key takeaway: Share Resolver rules with RAM.

stem: Which TWO practices reduce risk when changing production routing through automation? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Validate changes with Reachability Analyzer before and after deployment
Disable monitoring during changes to reduce noise
Apply changes to all Regions at once during peak traffic
Make manual console edits after the automated deployment
Deploy changes in stages with automated rollback on health checks

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Pre and post checks and staged rollouts with rollback limit the impact of routing mistakes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Disable monitoring during changes to reduce…: Disabling monitoring hides problems.
• Apply changes to all Regions at once during…: Global simultaneous changes maximize blast radius.
• Make manual console edits after the…: Manual edits cause drift.

Key takeaway: Validate and stage network changes.

stem: Branch offices connect via VPN to a virtual private gateway and must also reach each other through AWS. Which feature enables this hub-and-spoke pattern?

choices.text: NAT gateways only
AWS VPN CloudHub
Gateway endpoints
VPC peering mesh

explanation:
Why this is correct:
VPN CloudHub lets multiple sites connected to a VGW communicate with each other.

Why the other options are wrong:
• NAT gateways only: NAT gateways provide egress.
• Gateway endpoints: Gateway endpoints access S3 and DynamoDB.
• VPC peering mesh: Peering connects VPCs.

Key takeaway: Site-to-site through a VGW → VPN CloudHub.

stem: Multicast traffic is required between EC2 instances across VPCs for a trading application. Which service supports this?

choices.text: VPC peering connections only
Amazon CloudFront distributions
Application Load Balancer rules
Transit Gateway multicast domains

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Transit gateways support multicast domains for multicast traffic across attached VPCs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• VPC peering connections only: Peering does not support multicast.
• Amazon CloudFront distributions: CloudFront delivers content.
• Application Load Balancer rules: ALBs route HTTP.

Key takeaway: Multicast in AWS → TGW multicast.
